explanation: The H221Y substitution introduces a bulkier aromatic residue (40 Å³ volume increase) in the connection subdomain that, despite not directly contacting efavirenz, likely perturbs the conformational dynamics or indirect stabilization networks supporting the NNRTI-binding pocket located ~12 Å away. The loss of the positively charged imidazole ring (His) in favor of a neutral hydroxyl group eliminates local electrostatic interactions that may have helped organize the protein scaffold or stabilize water-mediated interactions critical for maintaining optimal inhibitor accommodation. The minimal predicted energetic penalty (ΔΔG ≈ 0 kcal/mol) suggests this is a subtle allosteric effect where the mutation subtly destabilizes the binding-competent conformation rather than creating direct steric clash with efavirenz.
